newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan group warns of cephalopods extinction.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan group warns of cephalopods extinction.

text.p: A Moroccan fishing group on Tuesday called for urgent measures to protect cephalopods, which it said risked extinction because of over exploitation, the official MAP news agency reported.

MAP quoted the Association des Cephalopodiers Marocains (ACM) as saying: "There is a dramatic decline in cephalopods catches (on the Atlantic coast) due largerly to an over exploitation of stocks...We want the authorities to take urgent measures to protect these species."
Cephalopods include octopus, squid and cuttlefish.
The group, which gathers 40 companies and operates 280 vessels, blamed foreign fishing fleets that it said caught more than allowed.
The group said its average catches of cephalopods were about 280 kg (616 pds) per day in the last nine months, down from 476 kg per day in the same period last year.
The ACM group said it plans "to launch a campaign aimed at halting the over-limit fishing of cephalopod species by foreign fleets."
Last year, the European Union and Morocco agreed to a four-year fisheries accord after Rabat insisted on lower Spanish and Portuguese fish catches, including cephalopods in Moroccan waters.
The accord allows 600 fishing boats from southern Spain, the Canary Islands and Portugal to operate in Moroccan waters, mainly on the Atlantic coast.
Under the deal the EU would pay Morocco $162.5 million a year in fees for fishing rights for the mainly Spanish fishing fleet.
